question: us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.rent-stabilization
definition: yes = a state (or D.C.) statute limits annual rent increases statewide or on a broad statewide class of units; no = the state preempts local rent control by statute or constitution and has no statewide limit; neither (no limit, local rent control allowed) or unconfirmed = unknown. State answer on 2026-01-01 outranks city ordinances.
summarySource: NMHC and NAA rent-control preemption tracking (2022-2025), Virginia Housing Commission study (June 2026), state code sites and Justia for each statute; searched 2026-09-28.

US-AZ.note: Preemption dates from 1981 and covers charter cities.

US-CA.cite: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (AB 1482, Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
US-CA.note: Caps increases at 5% plus local CPI or 10%, whichever is lower, on most units 15+ years old; exempts qualifying owner-noticed single-family homes and condos; sunsets 2030-01-01.

US-CO.note: HB23-1115, which would have repealed the preemption, passed the House in 2023 but did not become law.

US-DC.note: District-wide rent stabilization covers most pre-1976 units: CPI-W plus 2%, capped at 10%, once per 12 months; lower cap for registered elderly or disabled tenants.

US-FL.note: The 2023 Live Local Act removed the former housing-emergency exception effective 2023-07-01.

US-IL.note: Enacted 1997; repeal bills (e.g., SB 1260, 2025) have not passed.

US-KY.note: Only the General Assembly may enact rent control on private property.

US-LA.note: Lessor rights may not be altered except by state law (Acts 1977, No. 655); it is an implied rather than rent-specific preemption.

US-MA.cite: Mass. G.L. c. 40P (Rent Control Prohibition Act, 1994 Question 9)
US-MA.note: The Supreme Judicial Court removed a 2026 rent-control initiative from the ballot.

US-MO.note: Preemption was broadened in August 2025 to other landlord-tenant topics.

US-MS.note: Municipalities may not regulate residential rent without prior legislative approval.

US-MT.note: Express denial of local rent-control power added in 2023 (sources name SB 105 or HB 463); opponents said it was already prohibited.

US-NE.note: Signed 2025-04-07; takes effect three months after the 2025 session adjourned (operative date computed, not stated in results).

US-OH.note: HB 430 added an express preemption of local rent control and rent stabilization.

US-OR.note: Cap is 7% plus CPI; SB 611 (effective 2023-07-06) added a 10% ceiling; units under 15 years old are exempt; ORS 91.225 still preempts local rent control.

US-TX.note: Cities may impose rent control only in a disaster-declared housing emergency with the governor's approval.

US-UT.note: Local rent control requires express legislative approval.

US-VA.cite: Va. Code § 55.1-1200 et seq. (VRLTA supersession) with Dillon Rule
US-VA.note: No rent-specific preemption statute; localities lack authority because the VRLTA supersedes local landlord-tenant ordinances, and 2026 bills HB 278/SB 355 to authorize local rent regulation were sent to study.

US-WA.note: Cap is the lesser of 7% plus CPI or 10% over 12 months (9.683% for 2026); new construction under 15 years exempt; expires 2040-07-01; RCW 35.21.830 still preempts local rent control.

unknown.US-AK: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed (no preemption statute; no local ordinance in force).
unknown.US-AS: not-found: no rent-increase limit or preemption rule confirmed.
unknown.US-CT: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed through municipal fair rent commissions (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 7-148b) that review 'excessive' rents case by case; no annual numeric cap.
unknown.US-DE: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed (no preemption statute; the manufactured-home rent justification law covers only lot rents).
unknown.US-GU: not-found: no rent-increase limit or preemption rule confirmed.
unknown.US-HI: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed (no preemption statute; no local ordinance in force).
unknown.US-MD: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed (Montgomery County and Takoma Park have local caps).
unknown.US-ME: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed (Portland caps increases at CPI by local ordinance).
unknown.US-MN: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed only by voter approval in a general election under Minn. Stat. § 471.9996 (St. Paul and Minneapolis authority); otherwise preempted.
unknown.US-MP: not-found: no rent-increase limit or preemption rule confirmed.
unknown.US-NH: not-found: no statewide limit and no preemption statute found, but sources disagree on whether New Hampshire case law bars local rent control; see conflicts.
unknown.US-NJ: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed (more than 100 municipalities have rent-control ordinances).
unknown.US-NV: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed as far as found (no preemption statute located); state senior rent-cap bills (AB 298) were vetoed in 2023 and 2025.
unknown.US-NY: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed by local option: the Emergency Tenant Protection Act / Rent Stabilization Law is a state statute but limits increases only in NYC and localities that opt in (statewide opt-in since the 2019 HSTPA), so it is not a statewide or broad statewide-class limit.
unknown.US-PA: not-found: no statewide limit; sources disagree whether an express preemption statute exists (one cites 68 P.S. § 250.510, others say only the 1951 Landlord and Tenant Act and Dillon's Rule bar local caps); see conflicts.
unknown.US-PR: not-found: Puerto Rico's Reasonable Rents Act (Ley de Alquileres Razonables) was repealed by Law 57 of 1995, so there is no limit; no preemption rule found.
unknown.US-RI: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed (no preemption statute; 2025 statewide 4% cap bills S0580/H5264 failed).
unknown.US-VI: not-found: no rent-increase limit or preemption rule confirmed.
unknown.US-VT: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed (no preemption statute), though charter changes need legislative approval.
unknown.US-WV: not-found: no statewide limit; one low-quality source claims preemption under W. Va. Code ch. 37-6 without a section, not confirmed.
unknown.US-WY: local-allowed: no statewide limit; local rent control allowed per most sources (no express preemption statute found); one source claims preemption without a cite.

conflicts.readings: No express preemption; Dillon's Rule and the Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951 bar local caps per the Reading city solicitor (unknown) vs. an express preemption at 68 P.S. § 250.510 (no).
No state preemption, local rent control allowed vs. case law prohibits local rent control.
Express preemption under W. Va. Code ch. 37-6 (no section cited) vs. no preemption listed by NMHC-derived lists.
No express preemption statute, local rent control allowed vs. state law preempts local action.
Answered no: VRLTA supersession and Dillon Rule bar local rent control, but no rent-specific preemption statute; some lists omit Virginia from preempting states.
The 2023 preemption bill is reported as HB 463 in some sources and SB 105 in others; the answer (no) is the same.
